_supersedes_nothing: This file is ADDITIVE to paper/screen/access_recovery.json. Pass 1 recovered 4 records; this pass re-attacked the 16 it left behind and recovered 0. Both files are overlays; neither edits a sealed batch file.
_what_this_is: Second re-run of the access ladder over the SIXTEEN records left unreachable by paper/screen/access_recovery.json, driven by MACHINE endpoints rather than the web layer, on the hypothesis (stated in the task) that the PMC OA Web Service and the Europe PMC REST full-text endpoints would bypass the Cloudflare/bot obstructions that defeated pass 1. That hypothesis is now falsified for this sample and the falsification is recorded per record: none of the sixteen has a PMC deposit at all, so the PMC OA Web Service is not merely blocked but inapplicable, and Europe PMC returns HTTP 404 for fullTextXML and supplementaryFiles on all sixteen. Zero full texts were recovered. The bounding interval is therefore unchanged.
_does_not_edit_sealed_files: screen_batch_{A,B,C,D}.json and screen_reserve_R*.json are the screeners' sealed, git-timestamped submissions and are NOT modified. This file is an overlay with an EMPTY records[] array, so applying it changes no number; its value is the per-record endpoint ledger in still_unreachable[].endpoints_tried, which exists so the next operator does not repeat ~30 failed lookups per record.
_sources_permitted: PubMed Central / Europe PMC (search, fullTextXML, supplementaryFiles, annotations); NCBI esearch db=pmc; PMC ID converter; PMC OA Web Service; Unpaywall; OpenAlex; Semantic Scholar Graph API; Crossref registered text-mining, syndication and similarity-checking links; OpenAIRE; CORE v3; DOAJ; DataCite; arXiv; Zenodo; HAL; OSF preprints; PubMed LinkOut; the Internet Archive Wayback Machine CDX API and Internet Archive Scholar as public archives of pages that are themselves openly licensed.
_sources_refused: Sci-Hub, LibGen, Anna's Archive and every other unauthorised full-text source. None was fetched, not even to test whether it held a record; search results pointing at such hosts were discarded unread. No bot-detection or CAPTCHA challenge was circumvented or solved: Springer's client challenge, IEEE's script shell, ScienceDirect's 'are you a robot' captcha, DuckDuckGo's and Mojeek's bot challenges were all recorded as failures and left. No browser User-Agent was spoofed; every request identified itself as PhaseDx-screen/1.0 with a contact address. No new Wayback 'Save Page Now' snapshot was created, because that writes to a public archive.

_ladder_rerun_summary.note: Because nothing was recovered, records[] is empty and every endpoint in paper/screen/analysis/recompute_with_recovery.py returns exactly the numbers it returned before. The headline stays the bounding interval, per screen_protocol.md sec.7 rule 4.

_what_this_pass_adds: The PMC route is closed by absence, not by blocking: idconv returns no PMCID for any of the 16, and NCBI esearch on db=pmc returns 0 hits for all 16 by exact title AND by DOI. The PMC OA Web Service cannot be tried at all. This was the task's highest-prior route and it is now definitively excluded.

Europe PMC holds no body for any of the 16: fullTextXML and supplementaryFiles are HTTP 404 across the board, and a title search across ALL Europe PMC sources (including PPR preprints and bookXML) returns only the MED abstract record.

No preprint or repository copy exists for any of the 16: arXiv 0/16 on exact-title and loose queries, Zenodo 0/16, HAL 0/16, OSF 0/16, OpenAIRE has no fulltext instance for any, Unpaywall has_repository_copy is False for 15 of 16, and CORE's single hit (40147601) is a DOAJ metadata harvest whose advertised download URL returns HTTP 404.

The three known open-access-but-blocked records are CONFIRMED and the disclosure is strengthened: pubs.rsna.org, onlinelibrary.wiley.com and www.sciencedirect.com are blocked at the ORIGIN by this environment's browsing policy in a real browser (both the built-in Browser pane and the connected Chrome instance), not merely by publisher bot detection against scripted clients. academic.oup.com, link.springer.com and ieeexplore.ieee.org are blocked the same way. The obstruction is on our side of the wire.

One new lead: NLM's LinkOut marks the OUP full-text link for 39107903 (Dentomaxillofac Radiol) a 'free resource', contradicting Unpaywall/OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar/OpenAIRE. Uncorroborated, so NOT upgraded here, but it is the fourth record a screener on an unblocked network should test.

Two routes remain genuinely UNTRIED rather than failed, because the hosts were unreachable or the tool was broken in this environment: the fatcat API (api.fatcat.wiki, connection hangs), the Memento TimeTravel aggregator (HTTP 000, would cover archive.today), and general web search (WebSearch tool errored on every call; DuckDuckGo and Mojeek served CAPTCHAs that were not solved). The next operator should start there and with the six blocked publisher domains.
_positive_finding_search: The task's instruction to look for a POSITIVE as hard as for the absence was honoured, but it could not be exercised: coding a zero-image baseline as PRESENT requires a verbatim quote from the body, and no body was obtained for any of the sixteen. No record here is coded either way. Two abstracts contain material that would bear on the endpoints if the body were readable and are logged so they are not lost: 37222638's abstract describes a clinical-variables-only comparator model (AUC 0.741/0.772/0.675), which would bear on secondary endpoint S1 -- already noted by pass 1 -- and 42489954's abstract suggests a functional-connectivity-graph input, which would bear on eligibility (E-DERIV). Neither is coded, because an abstract is not evidence under this codebook.

_environment_limitation_statement: Three of the sixteen -- 37222638 (J Magn Reson Imaging, Unpaywall bronze OA, publisher PDF at onlinelibrary.wiley.com), 42153825 (Radiology, Unpaywall AND OpenAlex AND OpenAIRE all report hybrid OA under CC BY) and 40147601 (NeuroImage, gold OA, CC BY-NC-ND, confirmed keylessly by Elsevier's own coredata endpoint: openaccess=1, openaccessType=Full, and by DOAJ listing) -- are demonstrably open access and are unreachable ONLY because this execution environment cannot reach Wiley, RSNA or Elsevier. Pass 1 attributed this to publisher bot detection against scripted clients. Pass 2 establishes something stronger and more honest: all three domains, plus academic.oup.com, link.springer.com and ieeexplore.ieee.org, are blocked AT THE ORIGIN by this environment's own browsing policy, in the built-in browser pane and in a real connected Chrome instance alike. The obstruction is ours, not the literature's. Reporting these three as 'unreachable' without saying so would misattribute an environment limitation to the literature; reporting them as 'reachable' without having read them would be an unevidenced code. They are therefore counted as unreachable and this paragraph is the disclosure. A screener on an unblocked network should recover all three, taking the count from 16 to 13 and the rate from 29.6% to 24.1% (Wilson [14.6%, 36.9%]); if 39107903's LinkOut 'free resource' signal also holds, 12 and 22.2% (Wilson [13.2%, 34.9%]). Both are still above the 15% threshold, so the bounding interval remains the headline either way, and the headline is insensitive to this limitation.
